papers.title: How JWST is Revolutionizing Our View of Early Galaxy Formation
papers.authors: Rychard Bouwens
papers.abstract: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has been revolutionizing our understanding of early galaxy formation over its first four years of science operations. With un- precedented sensitivity, spatial resolution, and wavelength coverage from the near- to mid-infrared, JWST has enabled astronomers to identify hundreds of star-forming galaxies at redshifts z>~8 (within ~650 million years of the Big Bang) through strong spectral breaks and characterize these galaxies through sensitive spectroscopy. These capabilities have provided new insights into the stellar populations, neutral gas, nebular continuum emission, chemical enrichment, dust content, and ionization conditions of galaxies during cosmic dawn, revealing more numerous and brighter systems than anticipated from pre-JWST models. We discuss the implications of these discoveries for reionization, the buildup of stellar mass and metals, and the evolution of galaxy populations and luminosity functions. JWST is also revealing a new physical picture of early galaxies, characterized by compact, clumpy star formation, high gas fractions, and intense radiation fields. Despite much progress, many open questions remain, including the efficiency, intermittency, and stellar initial mass function (IMF) of early star formation, conditions in the interstellar medium (ISM), masses, and structure of the earliest galaxies, and the topology of reionization. Resolving these open questions will require lensing magnification, sensitive spectroscopy to > 5 micron, including with the Atacama Large Millimeter Array (ALMA), exploration to higher redshifts, and larger, more complete samples, helping to clarify how the first galaxies formed and evolved.

papers.title: EMRIs in Kerr Spacetime: The Role of Inclination Diffusion
papers.authors: Yael Alush, Nicholas C. Stone, Scott A. Hughes
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; High Energy Astrophysical Phenomena (astro-ph.HE); General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology (gr-qc)
papers.abstract: Extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs) are expected to be a major source of gravitational waves (GWs) for the future {\it Laser Interferometer Space Antenna} ({\it LISA}). An EMRI occurs when a compact object, driven by the emission of gravitational radiation, slowly inspirals into a massive black hole (MBH). The classical formation channel involves repeated two-body interactions within dense nuclear star clusters. However, both EMRI event rates and the expected distribution of their orbital parameters remain highly uncertain. A major source of this uncertainty is the poorly constrained ratio between gradually inspiraling EMRIs and direct plunges, which do not produce detectable GWs. While most studies of astrophysical EMRI production focus on the Schwarzschild limit, previous work examining the Kerr metric found that the spin of the central MBH can significantly affect the EMRI-to-plunge ratio. This enhancement depends sensitively on orbital inclination, yet earlier studies held inclination fixed. In this work, we develop the mathematical framework describing inclination evolution driven by two-body encounters evolving along Kerr geodesics. By implementing 3D diffusion into Monte Carlo simulations, we show that initially prograde orbits may evolve into retrograde states, thereby converting potential EMRIs into plunges or vice versa. We estimate the EMRI-to-plunge ratio and find that substantial MBH spin enhances the EMRI rate by a factor of $\sim 2.5$. Additionally, even for a non-spinning MBH, modeling the orbits as relativistic geodesics rather than Newtonian trajectories increases the number of EMRIs by a similar factor of $\sim 2.5$. The distribution of Kerr EMRI inclinations has a substantial prograde bias that may aid in identifying the subset of loss cone EMRIs within large future EMRI samples.

papers.title: The Dance of the Little Red Dots: Spectroscopy of Two Blue Companions at z = 3.9 and 5.5 Reveals Young, Metal-Poor Starbursts Merging with Their LRDs within a Few Hundred Myr
papers.authors: Fabio Pacucci, Pierluigi Rinaldi
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; Cosmology and Nongalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO); High Energy Astrophysical Phenomena (astro-ph.HE)
papers.abstract: The Little Red Dots (LRDs) are compact, red sources, abundant at $4 \lesssim z \lesssim 9$ and likely powered by massive black holes. Photometric studies have found blue companions around them, but none has yet been confirmed spectroscopically. This Letter presents the only two LRD-companion pairs with spectroscopy of both members in the literature: "Waltz" at $z = 3.9$ and "Tango" at $z = 5.5$, with projected separations of $3.6$ and $2.5$ kpc. Both companions lie at the redshift of their LRD, within $132 \, \rm km \, s^{-1}$ and $57 \, \rm km \, s^{-1}$, and are physically identical, but $524$ Myr apart: starbursts $\lesssim 50$ Myr old, metal-poor ($0.2 \, \rm Z_\odot$), dust-free, dynamically cold, and as bright as the LRDs themselves in the rest-frame UV. The LRD in Waltz hosts a $\approx 3 \times 10^{6} \, \rm M_\odot$ black hole accreting at half the Eddington rate, a factor of a few above the birth mass of a direct collapse black hole, and is embedded in gas as metal-poor as its companion. Orbital modeling shows that Tango is bound in $81\%$ of the allowed orbits and that Waltz is bound if its host halo exceeds $5 \times 10^{10} \, \rm M_\odot$. Both blue companions then merge with their respective LRD within a few hundred Myr. We conclude that we are observing what heavy seeding requires: a young black hole beside the metal-poor starburst that the synchronized-pair scenario predicts, in the last steps of a cosmic dance that ends in a merger, and in a galaxy seeded by its black hole.

papers.title: Wave Cold Dark Matter Can Reproduce the Radial Acceleration Relation in X-ray Elliptical Galaxies
papers.authors: Runyu Meng, Xiaobo Dong
papers.abstract: Wave cold dark matter (wave CDM) is a well-motivated variant within the collisionless CDM paradigm, in which the de~Broglie wavelengths of ultralight bosons become relevant on galactic scales. While many of the previous tests of wave CDM have focused on small-scale tensions involving solitonic cores and certain soliton--halo relations in galaxies, the radial acceleration relation (RAR) provides a complementary test: for a given baryonic mass distribution, it probes whether the DM halo can reproduce the observed total gravitational field. In this work we test wave CDM against the RAR using eight X-ray elliptical galaxies from the compilation of Lelli et al. We perform a suite of 3D Schrödinger--Poisson simulations and evolve the wave-CDM halos to virialized quasi-stationary states. For each galaxy and each adopted boson mass, we select the realization whose final snapshot most closely matches the empirical RAR. We find that the selected wave-CDM realizations for these elliptical galaxies can reproduce the RAR without including baryonic feedback or dark-matter self-interactions. At the boson mass $m_a=10^{-23}$eV, the combined fit to the eight galaxies gives $a_0=1.19\times10^{-10}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, consistent with the canonical value inferred from disk galaxies. When the boson mass is varied over $3\times 10^{-24}$ eV $\le m_a \le 2\times 10^{-23}$ eV, the best-fit value of $a_0$ changes by only $\sim 11\%$, and this variation shows no systematic trend with $m_a$. This insensitivity to boson mass arises because, over the radial range relevant for the RAR, the virialized halos are supported mainly by their velocity field, whereas the boson-mass-dependent quantum-pressure term is dynamically subdominant. These results show that wave CDM can reproduce the RAR in elliptical galaxies, and provide a new galactic-scale test of the model beyond the previous focus on solitonic cores.

papers.title: GroArnold: A Framework for Constructing Action-based Models for Triaxial Galaxies and Dark Matter Halos
papers.authors: Jian-Yu Gu, Xiao-Bo Dong, Shi-Yan Zhong, Run-Yu Meng
papers.abstract: Action-based distribution functions $f(\mathbf{J})$ provide a powerful description of stellar systems. Consequently, the construction of physically accurate and dynamically stable $f(\mathbf{J})$ for galactic components has emerged as a key challenge in the field. In this study, we present GroArnold, a computational framework designed to construct analytical $f(\mathbf{J})$ expressions for axisymmetric and triaxial galaxies and dark matter halos. The framework integrates modules for $N$-body initial condition generation, $N$-body simulation, angle--action variable estimation, and distribution-function fitting into a unified workflow. It supports a wide range of density profiles and kinematic properties, and is uniquely designed to generate stable $N$-body models for user-specified galactic systems, with the aim of obtaining an $f(\mathbf{J})$ that approximates a dynamically stable and physically consistent state. To this end, we extend the triaxial Stäckel Fudge method of the TACT code, implemented in our Nbody-TACT module, to enable action estimation directly from $N$-body gravitational potentials. GroArnold provides a robust and flexible tool for deriving numerically empirical, explicitly analytical distribution functions for user-specified galaxies or halos, thereby facilitating a wide range of practical $f(\mathbf{J})$-based modeling applications. In addition, it serves as a powerful tool for investigating the dynamics of realistic triaxial galaxies and halos beyond the scope of traditional spherical or axisymmetric models. We assessed the accuracy of the output $f(\mathbf{J})$ by comparing its predicted spatial and velocity distributions with those of the input $N$-body snapshot, and confirmed that it provides a reasonably accurate representation of the input. The code is modular, publicly available, and designed to support future extensions and adaptations.

papers.title: A Nonlinear General Implicit Runge-Kutta Integrator for Multifluid Charged Dust and Gas
papers.authors: Mengxuan Chen, Hui Li, Chong-Chong He, Benjamin D. Wibking, Mark R. Krumholz, Xue-Ning Bai
papers.abstract: Charged dust in magnetized gas is subject to aerodynamic drag and the Lorentz force, both of which can be difficult to model numerically in a fluid simulation where their characteristic timescales are shorter than the timestep set by the Courant condition. We present a two-stage general implicit Runge-Kutta (GIRK) source integrator for multifluid charged dust coupled to an ideal magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) gas, implemented in the open source GPU-accelerated quokka code. Drag and Lorentz forces are advanced together in one implicit source update, avoiding errors in the terminal drift that can arise when the two forces are advanced in separate substeps. The timestep is compared with a drag-Lorentz timescale to select between resolved and stiff branches. The resolved branch uses Gauss-Legendre coefficients, while the stiff branch uses a coefficient set designed to recover the terminal drift set by the drag-Lorentz balance. We also allow the dust stopping time and charge-to-mass ratio to depend on the evolving state, evaluating them separately at the two implicit stage states and solving the resulting nonlinear stage equations by Picard iteration. The source update conserves total gas-dust momentum, and its computational cost scales linearly with the number of dust species. Tests reproduce the expected drag damping and terminal drift, confirm the predicted gyromotion amplitude and phase errors, demonstrate accurate treatment of state-dependent source coefficients, and recover the expected wave, shock, and instability dynamics in dusty MHD flows.

papers.title: Substructure-enhanced Collisional Relaxation in Stellar Systems
papers.authors: Jian-Yu Gu, Xiao-Bo Dong, Run-Yu Meng
papers.abstract: Two-body collisional relaxation in stellar systems is conventionally estimated using the classical Chandrasekhar theory, in which a subject star is assumed to be embedded in a homogeneous medium of field stars and their velocity distribution taken to be isotropic and Gaussian. Real stellar systems, however, can exhibit pronounced spatial and kinematic substructures. We investigate how such substructures -- particularly the non-classical spatial inhomogeneity -- modify the two-body diffusion coefficient. We retain hyperbolic two-body encounters but generalize the encounter calculation by integrating explicitly over the spatial distribution $n(\mathbf{r})$, while evaluating the velocity contribution from the full distribution $f_v(\mathbf{v})$. This yields a separable tensor expression for the diffusion coefficient. We find that spatial substructure produces the dominant enhancement. The enhancement of the diffusion coefficient increases systematically as the effective fractal dimension $D_{\rm frac}$ decreases, $\log \zeta_r(D_\text{frac}) \sim \left(1-D_\text{frac}/3\right)^q$ with $q \approx 4.28$. For the observationally motivated case with $D_{\rm frac}\approx 1.5$, the enhancement is moderate, whereas substantially lower fractal dimensions produce much larger enhancements. In contrast, the anisotropic, power-law-tailed, and fractal-like velocity distributions modify the diffusion coefficient only by factors of order unity. Our representative substructured model yields enhancement ratios $\zeta_r\simeq3.45$ and $\zeta_v\simeq1.33$ when the measured particle-number trends are extrapolated to $N=10^{11}$, corresponding to an overall enhancement of $\zeta\simeq4.6$. Therefore, within the two-body encounter framework and the commonly used separable distribution functions, the enhanced collisional relaxation still has little impact on the mean-field nature of typical galactic systems.

papers.title: The convective-transition gap in 47 Tucanae with JWST
papers.authors: M. Scalco (1), L. R. Bedin (2), M. Libralato (2), M. Griggio (3), E. Vesperini (1), R. Gerasimov (4) ((1) Indiana University, (2) INAF-OAPD, (3) STScI, (4) University of Notre Dame)
papers.abstract: We report the detection of the convective-transition gap along the lower main sequence (MS) of the Galactic globular cluster (GC) 47 Tucanae using deep James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations. We analyse the stellar luminosity function (LF) in the vicinity of the gap location using two independent colour-magnitude diagrams (CMDs). In both cases, the LF is characterised by a narrow gap followed by a discontinuous increase in the stellar number counts, and presents an overall morphology qualitatively consistent with that reported in previous studies. By modelling the observed LFs with an empirical likelihood model, we estimate the statistical significance of the observed feature. Additional JWST passbands exhibit similar signatures, providing further evidence for the presence of a discontinuity.

papers.title: The connection between massive galaxies and their dark matter haloes from $z=0.25$ to $z \sim 4$ from the combined COSMOS, XMM-LSS and ECDF-S fields
papers.authors: Natalia Stylianou, Matt J. Jarvis, Rohan G. Varadaraj, Peter W. Hatfield, Joel Hamlett, Catherine L. Hale, Tariq Yasin
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; Cosmology and Nongalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)
papers.abstract: Understanding how galaxies populate and grow within dark matter haloes is essential for linking the observed evolution of galaxies to the hierarchical growth of structure. We present a galaxy clustering analysis using optical and near-infrared data from the UltraVISTA and VIDEO surveys covering $9.3$ deg$^2$ across the COSMOS, XMM-LSS and ECDF-S fields, $\sim 5\times$ larger than previous comparable studies, providing sufficient volume to determine the halo occupation of the most massive galaxies to $z\sim 4$. We measure the angular two-point correlation function for stellar-mass-selected galaxies over $0.25<z<4$ and by combining the three fields, we reduce the cosmic variance by a factor of $\sim2$ compared to the individual fields. The stellar-to-halo mass ratio peaks at a halo mass of $M_{h}\approx10^{12} {\rm M}_{\odot}$ and is a maximum at $z\sim 1$. For the most massive galaxies, the peak halo mass ($M_{h}^{\rm peak}$) increases from $z=1\rightarrow 0$, while the peak stellar mass in such haloes remains approximately constant, indicating that at $z<1$ massive galaxy formation becomes less efficient. We also find a steady increase in the satellite fraction since $z\sim 1$, from which we infer that massive halos continue to grow hierarchically while their central galaxies experience suppressed stellar-mass growth. We suggest this is due to the central massive galaxies having their growth controlled by feedback from active galactic nuclei feedback, likely from low-power stochastic radio emission.

papers.title: MOSS III: MeerKATs view on the galaxy populations in two massive galaxy clusters
papers.authors: Robert Kincaid, Mark Sargent, Pascale Jablonka, Bruno Slaus, Viral Parekh, Shishir Sankhayan, Sameer Salunke, Jean-Paul Kneib
papers.abstract: The MeerKAT Observations of the Saraswati Supercluster (MOSS) is an ongoing project attempting to study the radio and optical properties of the core region of the Saraswati supercluster (z = 0.28) and will eventually entail a full survey of the entire supercluster region. Here we use radio catalogs from previous deep pilot MeerKAT L-band (1.28 GHz) observations (angular resolution of 8 arcsec) of the core region of the Saraswati supercluster. The region hosts two galaxy clusters representing distinct environments: The most massive cluster Abell 2631, and the second most massive cluster ZwCl2341, that is significantly more dynamically active. The deep radio catalogs of these clusters were combined with spectroscopic redshifts (mainly from DESI DR1 and SDSS DR16) and optical photometry catalogs of the cluster member galaxy source population. We use these redshifts together with the 1.4GHz MeerKAT flux densities to derive the dust-free star-formation rate (SFR) and evaluate various trends in the radio SFG and AGN galaxy populations. We find that the actively merging cluster ZwCL2341 has an increased star-forming galaxy population compared to A2631 with up to 4 times more star-forming galaxies. When looking at SFG-related radio processes we see s enhanced SF-related activity in ZwCL2341 with SF-related radio processes dominates entirely over AGN-related radio processes. This suggests that dynamically active environments associated with cluster assembly, such as mergers, have enhanced SF radio-activity and increased SFG (both radio and non-radio) galaxy population compared to lesser active systems.

papers.title: Are Broad Mg II Galaxies Fading AGN?
papers.authors: Stephanie M. LaMassa, Michael Eracleous, Jessie Runnoe, Benny Trakhtenbrot, Gisella de Rosa
papers.abstract: We analyzed a sample of 494 galaxies from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) I-IV that have unusual properties. They display broadened Mg II $\lambda$2798 line emission, as would be expected of Type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGN). However, they have weak or absent broad Balmer lines though broadened Balmer lines often accompany broadened ultraviolet lines in Type 1 AGN spectra. We performed a spectral decomposition of these "broad Mg II galaxies'' to assess whether they can be considered fading AGN. The Balmer lines are more responsive to changes in the AGN continuum than the Mg II line. As the AGN power source fades, broad H$\beta$ and then H$\alpha$ will weaken and eventually disappear, leaving broad Mg II as a signpost of a more active past. In support of this interpretation, we found that broad Mg II galaxies have weaker AGN luminosities and lower accretion rates (parameterized by the Eddington ratio) than typical Type 1 quasars from SDSS. The Eddington ratio of broad Mg II galaxies are similar to dim-state changing-look AGN, with an average value $\lesssim$1\%, which is the threshold at which the inner region of a geometrically thin accretion disk is thought to evaporate and be replaced by a geometrically thick radiatively inefficient accretion flow in stellar-mass black holes. Broad Mg II galaxies may represent the penultimate stage in a changing-look AGN sequence prior to the complete disappearance of all broad lines.

papers.title: SQuIGGLE: Radio AGN Found Predominantly in Young, Gas-rich Post-starburst Galaxies at z ~ 0.7
papers.authors: Vincenzo R. D'Onofrio, Justin S. Spilker, Krista L. Smith, Rachel Bezanson, Robert Feldmann, Alex J. Geiger, Andy D. Goulding, Jenny E. Greene, Mariska Kriek, Anika Kumar, Yuanze Luo, Desika Narayanan, David J. Setton, Katherine A. Suess, Margaret E. Verrico, Pengpei Zhu
papers.abstract: The processes that rapidly quench massive galaxies and maintain their quiescence remain poorly understood. Substantial molecular gas reservoirs can survive this shutdown in post-starburst galaxies, raising the question of what prevents the remaining gas from efficiently forming stars. We present deep, subarcsecond VLA 6 GHz observations of 52 massive SQuIGGLE post-starburst galaxies at $z\sim0.7$ to test the prevalence and mechanical impact of radio activity during the gas-rich post-burst phase. We detect 6 GHz continuum emission in 18/52 galaxies ($\approx$35\%), spanning $\log(L_{1.4\,{\rm GHz}}/{\rm W\,Hz^{-1}})\simeq23.0$--$25.0$ and generally exceeding the contributions expected from ongoing star formation and the fading starburst, favoring an AGN origin. Ancillary data at other wavelengths provide little evidence for a population of luminous, radiatively efficient AGN, suggesting that these sources are instead dominated by comparatively weak, mechanically powered radio AGN. Radio activity is strongly concentrated within the first $\sim$200 Myr post-burst and is predominantly associated with galaxies retaining substantial gas reservoirs. Above a common radio luminosity threshold, the radio detection fraction is enhanced by a factor of $\approx$2.5 relative to the radio AGN candidate fraction in mass- and redshift-matched quiescent LEGA-C galaxies, primarily due to lower power sources. For efficient jet--ISM coupling, the inferred mechanical power could supply the approximate energy required to unbind the molecular gas on timescales comparable to its observed decline. Together, these results identify a population of radiatively inefficient AGN hosted predominantly by young, gas-rich post-starburst galaxies at $z\sim0.7$ and suggest that they may have a role in maintaining inefficient star formation.

papers.title: Emergence of high-mass stars in complex fiber networks (EMERGE) VII. Multi-Tracer Column Density Synthesis
papers.authors: Alvaro Hacar, Andrea Socci, Mario Tafalla, Francesca Bonanomi
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; Instrumentation and Methods for Astrophysics (astro-ph.IM)
papers.abstract: Obtaining accurate estimates of the gas column density $\mathrm{N(H_2)}$ is crucial to determine the physical conditions of the molecular gas in the Interstellar Medium. This paper introduces the "Multi-Tracer Column Density Synthesis" (MT-CDS) technique, a new empirical approach to derive high dynamic-range column density maps with interferometers such as ALMA. We have compared the integrated intensity maps of two density selective tracers, namely HNC (1-0) and $\mathrm{N_2H^+}$ (1-0), obtained with IRAM-30m with ancillary Herschel column density estimates in seven star-forming regions in Orion and derived individual temperature-corrected conversion factors for each of these tracers. We applied these conversion factors obtained at low-resolution into similar high sensitivity ALMA observations to derive independent column density maps describing both the low $N_\mathrm{HNC}\mathrm{(H_2)}$ and high $N_\mathrm{N_2H^+}\mathrm{(H_2)}$ column density components at high spatial resolution (4.5"). We also combined these independent maps into estimates for the total gas column density gas $N_\mathrm{tot}\mathrm{(H_2)}$ sampling more than two orders of magnitude in column density between $\sim 10^{21.5}-10^{23.5}$ cm$^{-2}$. A comparison with independent ArTeMiS column density maps at intermediate resolution (8") shows typical deviations of $\lesssim$0.2 dex from our MT-CDS gas column density estimates. We obtained individual column density maps in five of our targets at $\sim$2000 au resolution in which ALMA observations were available, that is a factor of $\sim$5 better than originally calibrated. These results demonstrate the potential of this MT-CDS technique to retrieve accurate, high dynamic range $N\mathrm{(H_2)}$ total gas column density estimates at interferometric resolution combining multiple molecular line tracers.

papers.title: Galactic Outflows and Star-Formation Quenching: A JWST Perspective
papers.authors: Rebecca L. Davies, Sirio Belli
papers.abstract: Outflows driven by active galactic nuclei (AGN) are widely considered a key mechanism for regulating and quenching star formation in massive galaxies. However, direct observational evidence linking outflows to quenching has remained elusive for decades. This article reviews recent findings for massive galaxies at cosmic noon ($z\sim 2$), based on sensitive James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations tracing both star formation histories (through Balmer absorption lines) and neutral outflows (through blueshifted NaID absorption). Neutral outflows are found in $\sim$ 25 - 50% of massive ($\log(M_*/M_\odot)>$ 10) galaxies, independent of star formation rate. Outflows from star-forming galaxies are consistent with being powered by star-formation and/or AGN activity, whereas outflows from quiescent systems are generally attributed to current or previous AGN activity. There is growing evidence that recent rapid quenching of star-formation is associated with powerful AGN-driven outflows with mass loading factors $\eta \gtrsim$ 1 - 10. The neutral gas dominates the outflow mass budget but in most cases its velocity is below the halo escape velocity, indicating that this gas may form part of a galactic fountain. Detections of neutral gas inflows and residual cold gas reservoirs in quiescent galaxies suggest that other feedback mechanisms such as AGN heating are required to keep galaxies quenched over long timescales. We highlight the potential of multiphase outflow measurements to constrain feedback models, describe the main systematic uncertainties in mass outflow rate measurements, and discuss how the $z\sim 2$ results inform our understanding of the formation of the earliest massive quiescent galaxies.

papers.title: The Contribution of Mergers and Accretion to Dark Matter Halo Assembly: An Excursion Set Theory Approach
papers.authors: Hamed Kameli
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; Cosmology and Nongalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)
papers.abstract: We study the relative contributions of mergers and accretion to the assembly of dark matter haloes within the framework of Excursion Set Theory (EST). We extend a variance-discretized merger-tree algorithm, which recursively reconstructs all branches of a complete merger tree and introduces a merger-ratio criterion for distinguishing mergers from accretion. The method is validated by comparing the resulting progenitor distributions with the analytical conditional first up-crossing distribution, showing excellent agreement over a wide range of halo masses and redshifts. We find that the accretion contribution depends strongly on the adopted merger-ratio threshold. For large merger ratios ($MR=0.1$--$0.25$), accretion accounts for up to $\sim70\%$ of the mass growth of massive haloes, whereas including all resolved mergers ($MR=10^{-6}$) reduces the accretion contribution to $\sim40\%$. These values are in good agreement with previous N-body simulation results. The accreted mass exhibits a nearly self-similar distribution in the mass-redshift plane, with the dominant contribution arising from progenitors in the range $10^{-3}M_0 \lesssim M \lesssim 10^{-1}M_0$ and predominantly at $0.5 \lesssim z \lesssim 2$. Our results demonstrate that EST-based merger trees provide an accurate and computationally efficient framework for investigating halo assembly and quantifying the relative roles of mergers and accretion in hierarchical structure formation.

papers.title: Deep X-ray View of a Distant Protocluster Anchored by a Quasar at $z=6.63$: No Evidence for Enhanced X-ray AGN Activity
papers.authors: Shouyi Wang, Feige Wang, Jinyi Yang, Bin Luo, Xiangyu Jin, Fan Zou, Jaclyn B. Champagne, Xiaohui Fan, Elaina Malczewski, Fabio Vito, Xue-Bing Wu, Eduardo Bañados, Fuyan Bian, Thomas Connor, Tiago Costa, Anna-Christina Eilers, Emanuele Paolo Farina, Joseph F. Hennawi, Hyunsung D. Jun, Jiang-Tao Li, Chiara Mazzucchelli, Klaudia Protušová, Fabian Walter, Zhibo Yu, Minghao Yue
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; High Energy Astrophysical Phenomena (astro-ph.HE)
papers.abstract: Whether dense environments accelerate SMBH growth during cosmic reionization remains uncertain because X-ray constraints on $z>6$ protoclusters are rare. We analyze $\sim865$ ks of Chandra observations of J0910-0414 quasar field, a massive protocluster at $z=6.63$. We construct a catalog of 251 X-ray sources and search for AGN among 21 spectroscopically confirmed members, excluding the central quasar. This is the first systematic X-ray AGN census in a $z>6$ protocluster; none of the members is individually detected. Stacking all members ($\sim17$ Ms total exposure) yields no significant signal and limits the average rest-frame 2-10 keV luminosity to $\langle L_{\rm 2-10~keV}\rangle\leq9.54\times10^{42}~\rm erg~s^{-1}$. The null result gives a central 90% Jeffreys upper bound of $f_{\rm AGN}<0.09$. After accounting for the spatially varying sensitivity, the field Compton-thin X-ray luminosity function predicts $N_{\rm exp,field}=0.0356$ AGN in the surveyed volume. Assuming the overdensity profile of AGNs in this protocluster is the same as that of galaxies determined by Wang et al. (2024), the expected AGN count becomes $N_{\rm exp}=0.131$. Zero detections then imply a one-sided 90% upper limit of $\eta_{\rm rel}<17.5$ on any additional X-ray AGN enhancement beyond that associated with the galaxy overdensity. Although $\eta_{\rm rel}<17.5$ permits more than an order-of-magnitude enhancement, the data show no significant excess of X-ray-detectable AGN in J0910-0414 protocluster. The present X-ray data may miss heavily obscured, intrinsically X-ray-weak, or intermittently accreting SMBHs; the non-detection therefore does not rule out AGNs among the member galaxies.

papers.title: A JWST View of Cosmic Star Formation from $z\sim0$ to 9 with Hydrogen Recombination Lines in the COSMOS and GOODS-N fields
papers.authors: Shuqi Fu, Linhua Jiang, Christopher J. Conselice, Zijian Zhang, Danyang Jiang, Jie Chen, Louis Quilley, Fengwu Sun, Ronaldo Laishram, Alberto Traina, Bahareh S. Salmasi, Duncan Austin
papers.abstract: We combine wide-area COSMOS-3D observations with deeper GOODS-N data from JWST/NIRCam F444W wide-field slitless spectroscopy to trace cosmic star formation over $z\sim0$--9. The observations cover approximately $0.33~\mathrm{deg}^2$ in COSMOS and $60.9~\mathrm{arcmin}^2$ in GOODS-N, with typical $3\sigma$ integrated line-flux limits of $3.2\times10^{-18}$ and $1.04\times10^{-18}~\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,cm^{-2}}$, respectively. The common $3.9$--$5.0\,\mu$m wavelength window probes Br$\alpha$, Br$\beta$, Pa$\alpha$, Pa$\beta$, H$\alpha$, and H$\beta$ across the local Universe, cosmic noon, and reionization. Our final sample contains 9146 galaxies, including 7883 in COSMOS and 1263 in GOODS-N. COSMOS constrains luminous emitters, while GOODS-N extends the luminosity functions toward fainter sources. We measure dust-corrected line luminosities, account for line-detection completeness, and convert the six lines to equivalent H$\alpha$ luminosities assuming Case B recombination. Schechter fits reveal an increase in the characteristic H$\alpha$-equivalent luminosity toward cosmic noon. Integrating the resulting star formation rate functions above $0.24\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, we trace the cosmic star formation rate density from the local Universe to reionization. The combined Brackett, Paschen, and Balmer measurements are broadly consistent with the canonical UV- and IR-based cosmic star formation history at $z\lesssim6$. Fixed-slope tests show that the H$\beta$ estimate at $z\sim8$ remains sensitive to the external photometric faint-end constraint and extrapolation below our spectroscopic limit. These measurements provide complementary constraints on the distribution and integrated rate of star formation across cosmic time.

papers.title: Hot Molecular Hydrogen in Galaxies at Redshift ~ 0.2-1.5 Revealed by JWST
papers.authors: Jie Chen, Linhua Jiang, Shuqi Fu, Zijian Zhang, Danyang Jiang, Jing Wang, Ran Wang, Darshan Kakkad
papers.abstract: Molecular hydrogen (H$_2$) is the fundamental component of the molecular gas reservoir that fuels star formation and black hole growth. While prominent hot H$_2$ emission ($\gtrsim 1000$ K) has been explored in nearby galaxies, its excitation mechanisms at higher redshifts remain poorly constrained. We present a systematic study of hot molecular gas traced via ro-vibrational H$_2$ emitters at z~0.2-1.5 using JWST slitless spectroscopy. Exploiting JWST's great sensitivity to near-infrared H$_2$ ro-vibrational transitions such as H$_2$ 1-0 S(1), we build a sample of 144 H$_2$-luminous galaxies and characterize their multi-wavelength properties. About 96.5% and 80% of these galaxies are detected in the radio and far-infrared (FIR) bands, respectively, and their hot H$_2$ emission strongly correlates with the radio and FIR radiation. Based on radio excess, X-ray emission, and optical diagnostics, 62 sources (43%) exhibit significant AGN activity. The H$_2$ line luminosities of the sample show a sublinear dependence on radio luminosity, while the relation between the H$_2$ luminosities and total infrared luminosities is approximately linear after excluding the radio-excess sources. These scaling relations suggest that star formation provides a baseline contribution to hot H$_2$ excitation, while radio-excess sources require an additional contribution from AGN-related processes such as jet- or wind-driven shocks. These results reveal a multi-channel excitation scenario and shed new light on the interplay between star formation, AGN activity, and the interstellar medium during galaxy evolution.

papers.title: Large-scale Environmental Dependence of AGN Activity Revealed by JWST Pa$α$ Emitters
papers.authors: Danyang Jiang, Linhua Jiang, Shuqi Fu, Zijian Zhang, Jie Chen, Chenxi Bao, Yihe Wang, Junya Arita, Darshan Kakkad, Jan-Torge Schindler
papers.abstract: The role of the large-scale environment in regulating AGN activity remains an open question. We investigate the Mpc-scale environments of 70 AGNs at $z=1.1$-$1.5$ using a highly complete sample of 3,419 Pa$\alpha$ emitters with accurate spectroscopic redshifts from JWST slitless spectroscopic survey. This dataset allows us to robustly trace the environments and quantify the environmental dependence of AGN properties. We measure the eighth-nearest-neighbor surface density of Pa$\alpha$ emitters around each AGN, probing $\sim$1.5 pMpc scale environments. We find that this environmental density exhibits a weak positive correlation with radio luminosity. Radio-bright AGNs tend to reside in statistically denser environments than their radio-faint counterparts. The environmental density also has a positive correlation with the Eddington ratio and a weak negative correlation with the central black hole mass, implying more efficient black hole accretion in dense environments. We construct Pa$\alpha$ luminosity functions (LFs) in AGN environments and find that they are systematically elevated relative to the field Pa$\alpha$ LF. In addition, their faint-end slopes are shallower, suggesting accelerated galaxy growth and enhanced quenching of star formation. As Pa$\alpha$ emitters trace gas-rich, star-forming galaxies, our results support a scenario in which the large-scale cold gas promotes AGN activity at cosmic noon.

papers.title: Simulations of Dust Content and Attenuation in $z=5-15$ Galaxies
papers.authors: Dhruv T. Zimmerman, Jed McKinney, Desika Narayanan, Caitlin M. Casey, John Chisholm, Alex M. Garcia, Michelle C. Jecmen, Jessica Kelley-Derzon, Federico Marinacci, Julian B. Muñoz, Laura V. Sales, Ethan Savitch, Paul Torrey
papers.abstract: Correctly modeling the dust attenuation law in galaxies is essential to properly inferring their growth and physical properties. With the rapid discovery of $z>6$ galaxies by JWST and lack of constraints on the properties of dust at these redshifts, we must turn to theoretical models to predict the properties of dust at these redshifts. In this paper, we develop a theoretical foundation for the nature of high-redshift attenuation laws. We analyze $107$ cosmological zoom-in simulations of galaxies run with the SMUGGLE galaxy formation model. SMUGGLE includes an explicitly modeled multiphase interstellar medium and a state-of-the-art dust model with a self-consistently evolving dust grain size distribution. We forward model these simulations with the radiative transfer package POWDERDAY to produce synthetic spectra and attenuation curves for a set of $z=5-15$, $M_*\sim10^{6.5}-10^{10}\; \mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ galaxies. We find evidence for flatter attenuation curves than the commonly used locally-calibrated literature attenuation laws assumed when modeling high-redshift galaxies. The vast majority of our attenuation curves also lack the 2175 Angstrom absorption feature. Our attenuation laws do not evolve strongly over $z=15-5$, which we attribute to relatively constant fractions of small grains up to $z=4$ in our simulations. We present a set of simulation-informed priors on dust attenuation law parameterization that could be implemented in SED fitting codes. There is an anti-correlation between galaxy mass and attenuation curve slope and positive correlation between galaxy mass and $A_V$, which we attribute to dust growth becoming efficient in our massive galaxies with $\log{M_*/\mathrm{M}_{\odot}}\gtrsim9$ and with ISM conditions above a critical metallicity threshold.

papers.title: Barflow: Modeling Gas Kinematics of Bar-Driven Flows
papers.authors: Seungwon Baek, Woong-Tae Kim, Taehyun Kim, Dajeong Jang, SungWon Kwak
papers.abstract: We present self-consistent $N$-body/hydrodynamical simulations of isolated, Milky Way-like galaxies with stellar and gaseous disks. By varying the initial gas fraction, we find that gas delays bar formation and, in the most gas-rich model, suppresses it by exciting higher-order spiral modes and promoting early central mass growth. Once a bar forms, continued gas inflow and gravitational torques weaken the bar and inhibit its secular slowdown, keeping bars in the gas-bearing models shorter and predominantly in the fast-bar regime, while the gas-free bar evolves into the slow-bar regime. Stars and gas respond differently to the same barred potential. While the mean stellar velocity field is well described by a smooth bisymmetric pattern, the cold and warm gas follow elongated, $x_1$-like streamlines with sharp shock-induced velocity transitions, producing sawtooth-like radial and archlike tangential velocity profiles. Despite these strong noncircular motions, their azimuthally averaged tangential velocities closely follow the circular velocity over most of the disk. By contrast, the hot gas is dominated by stellar feedback and thermal pressure and is largely decoupled from the ordered bar-driven flow. To describe these bar-driven gas flows, we introduce the barflow model, a phenomenological description of non-sinusoidal gas streaming motions with a radially varying shock-front phase. Mock line-of-sight velocity-fitting experiments show that the barflow model recovers the intrinsic rotation curve, bar-driven velocity perturbations, and radial gas transport more accurately than the conventional bisymmetric model.

papers.title: Microcaustics: Fast GPU-Accelerated Dynamical Microlensing of Time-Dependent Extended Sources
papers.authors: Joshua Fagin, Connor Stone, James Hung-Hsu Chan, Sophia Miskiewicz, Henry Best, Paras Sharma, Matthew O'Dowd, Laurence Perreault-Levasseur, Yashar Hezaveh, Simon Birrer
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; Instrumentation and Methods for Astrophysics (astro-ph.IM)
papers.abstract: Gravitational microlensing probes unresolved quasar accretion disc structure and compact objects in lens galaxies and is an important systematic in strong-lens time-delay cosmography. Most analyses use static microlensing map simulations because evolving individual microlenses and caustics is computationally prohibitive. We present Microcaustics, a GPU-accelerated Python package built on PyTorch for dynamical microlensing of time-dependent extended sources in strong gravitational lenses. It combines a local-exact/far-field deflection solver, source-directed lens-plane scouting with temporal reuse, and biquadratic inverse polygon mapping (IPM). GPU batching and fused Triton rasterization accelerate the calculation, while binary caustic labels track source-centred crossings. Across three simulated quadruply lensed quasar systems, our package generates a 10-year, 147-frame multiband light curve in an amortized median of 0.68 s (0.88 s with labels) on a consumer GPU with a median light-curve RMSE of 0.35 mmag, while recovering every reference source-centred caustic crossing. At comparable map accuracy, the batched throughput is 780 times higher than that of a recent CUDA IPM implementation and extrapolates to a speedup of millions relative to classic GPU-D. We demonstrate that our IPM converges as $N_{\rm ray}^{-0.84}$, approaching the idealized $N_{\rm ray}^{-1}$ convergence rate of piecewise-affine IPM and improving upon the $N_{\rm ray}^{-1/2}$ inverse ray-shooting rate. We also introduce a GPU-resident general relativistic and reverberating quasar source model and demonstrate our method with an evolving supernova source. These advances make fully dynamical stellar fields practical for Bayesian and simulation-based inference.

papers.title: Large dust grains escaping from a supernova remnant
papers.authors: Evgenii O. Vasiliev
papers.abstract: Dust grains produced in the supernova (SN) ejecta at early ages are partially destroyed in hot gas of the SN remnant. Large grains owing to their inertia can overtake the forward shock front of the remnant and move through the ambient interstellar medium. Using one-dimensional gas dynamics including the dust destruction we study the transport of dust grains inside the SN remnant and the ambient medium. Here we estimate the surviving and escaping mass fractions depending on the cut-off (maximum) size in a power-law distribution of grain sizes. We found that these fractions follow closely each other at late age of the SN remnant, i.e. almost all grains, which have survived in the remnant, leave it for the ambient interstellar medium. At the age of 30 kyr -- the onset of the radiative phase with density $n\sim 1$ cm$^{-3}$ with solar metallicity -- the escaping/surviving mass fractions for the cut-off size of several microns reach about $0.7-0.8$. The major part of these grains have size larger than $1~\mu$m and initially located at distances $\gtrsim 0.2$ of the ejecta core radius. Later dust grains at velocity of several hundreds km/s escaping the remnant continue to be destroyed due to kinetic sputtering in the interstellar medium. Grains with sizes of several microns are destroyed marginally and therefore will survive in the interstellar gas. After decelerating of grains in the medium the surviving mass fraction of grains produced in the SN remnant, which evolves in an ambient gas with $n$ from 1 to 100 cm$^{-3}$, is from $\sim 0.5$ to $\sim 0.3$, respectively, for the cut-off grain size $a_{cut} = 10~\mu$m. A decrease of the cut-off size in the distribution results in lower surviving mass fraction.

papers.title: Strong gravitational lensing with Euclid
papers.authors: Alessandro Sonnenfeld (Shanghai Jiao Tong University)
papers.abstract: Euclid data is going to lead to the discovery of approximately 10^5 new strong gravitational lenses, thereby increasing the number of known lenses by a factor of 30. Such an impressive jump has the potential to revolutionise the field of strong lensing, by covering an ever-increasing range in the parameter space occupied by the lenses and lensed sources, and by uncovering rare and precious strong lens systems. The first quick data release of Euclid has already revealed hundreds of lenses, giving us a taste of what the final Euclid strong lens sample might look like. These lenses include a variety of objects acting as deflectors, from isolated galaxies to clusters, from early-type galaxies to edge-on disks. As many as four double-source plane lenses, in which one foreground object lenses two galaxies at two different redshifts, have already been discovered. As more data are acquired, it might become possible to detect the strong lensing signature of dwarf galaxy satellites, and to find lenses with an unusually large number of images. In this paper, we try to anticipate the kind of discoveries that these data will bring along.

papers.title: A heterogeneous set of unusual quasars selected from astrometry and broad-band photometry
papers.authors: C. Cheng (DAWN, NBI), K. Valeckas (DAWN, NBI, NOT, ESO), L. Christensen (DAWN, NBI), A. Henderson de la Fuente (NOT, Uni. Oxford), L. Fuglsang (NBI, NOT, Uni. Lyon), V. Vuolteennaho (NOT, Uni. Oulo), Pyykkinen (NOT, Uni. Turku), R. H. Rasmussen (NOT, Uni. Aarhus), S. Bijavara Seshashayana (NOT, Uni. Malmø), J. P. U. Fynbo (DAWN, NBI)
papers.abstract: The aim of this study is to explore methods for how to identify new quasars with different properties with regard to reddening, redshift, the presence of broad absorption lines from outflows, or other rare properties affecting the broad-band colours. We use Gaia-based astrometric pre-selection to study only sources that have zero parallax and zero proper motion within errors. We subsequently match these sources with information from wide-area photometric surveys and build colour-colour diagrams. Based on these diagrams we select targets for follow-up spectroscopy. In the subsequent analysis we also apply observations from SPHEREx to firmly establish redshifts. We secure spectroscopic observations for 24 sources. Of these, three are found to be stars and the remaining 21 are classified as quasars spanning a redshift range from z=0.139 to z=3.732. The majority of the sources located away from the normal quasar locus in colour-colour diagrams are found to be broad-absorption-line quasars. A single source, the lowest redshift source at z=0.139, is reminiscent of the so-called Little Red Dots found at high redshifts with JWST. Using the simple procedure followed here it is possible to locate previously undiscovered quasars with interesting properties, in particular Broad Absorption Line quasars and quasars with unusual extinction.

papers.title: PDRs4All XXIII. JWST-MIRI template spectra of PAHs in the Orion Bar obtained with blind signal separation
papers.authors: P. Amiot, O. Berné, J. Roux-Morin, I. Schroetter, C. Boersma, A. Fuente, J. R. Goicoechea, E. Habart, A. Maragkoudakis, T. Onaka, E. Peeters, M. Robberto, A.G.G.M Tielens, D. Van De Putte, S. Vicente
papers.abstract: The aromatic infrared bands (AIBs) are observed in a wide variety of astrophysical sources, and now in unprecedented detail by the James Webb space telescope (JWST). These bands are generally attributed to the emission from polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAHs). Our aim is to extract mid-infrared AIB template spectra from JWST observations of the Orion Bar photo-dissociation region that can be used to derive PAH properties from observations of other objects. We used the JWST MIRI-MRS observations from the PDRs4All program. We first isolated the AIBs from the data using a multi-component fitting approach. We then applied a non-negative matrix factorization to the isolated AIB spectra and extracted two templates, named AIBirrad and AIBshield following previous work. The spatial distribution and spectral characteristics of these two spectra suggest that they originate from two chemical distinct populations. We interpret AIBirrad as emission originating from a PAH population strongly exposed to ultra-violet (UV) radiation and mainly composed of large, compact ionized PAHs. Conversely, AIBshield is interpreted as originating from a more shielded population of PAHs, which is less exposed to the UV by being more embedded in the cloud. This population consists of small, asymmetric and mainly neutral PAHs with bonded aliphatic side groups. These templates can serve to analyze PAH emission in a wide variety of objects observed with MIRI-MRS.

papers.title: Sleeping or Dead? Probing the Quenching Mechanism of JWST Dormant Galaxies at z > 3 with ALMA
papers.authors: Mengyuan Xiao, Songnan Qi, Pascal A. Oesch, Longji Bing, Miroslava Dessauges-Zavadsky, Andreas L. Faisst, Mahsa Sanati, Rashmi Gottumukkala, Gabriel Brammer, David Elbaz, Robert Feldmann, Yoshinobu Fudamoto, Lucas C. Kimmig, Benjamin Magnelli, Rui Marques-Chaves, Anurag Amol Sawarkar, Sune Toft, Francesco Valentino, Christina C. Williams
papers.abstract: JWST has revealed a population of "dormant'' galaxies at z>3 with strong Balmer breaks and weak emission lines, whose star formation appears to have declined only recently. Whether these galaxies are undergoing a lasting transition toward quiescence or merely experiencing a temporary suppression of star formation remains unclear. We investigate their molecular gas content using archival ALMA observations of [CII]158um and CO rotational transitions. Starting from all publicly available JWST/NIRSpec prism observations and using joint spectrophotometric fitting, we construct a parent sample at z>3 and log(Mstar/Msun)>9.5 in the ALMA-accessible COSMOS, UDS, and GOODS-South fields. Our final sample comprises 7 dormant galaxies and 15 quiescent galaxies with ALMA constraints on their molecular gas content (mostly 3 sigma upper limits). We find that dormant galaxies exhibit systematically lower star formation rates averaged over the past 10Myr (SFR10Myr) than over the past 100Myr (SFR100Myr), supporting a recent rapid decline in their star formation. For the ~70% of the sample with sufficiently constraining ALMA observations, their molecular gas fractions lie at least ~0.3-2dex below those expected for main-sequence galaxies. Moreover, the molecular gas fractions of dormant galaxies show no systematic difference from those of quiescent galaxies in our sample. This indicates that dormant galaxies have already reached a gas-poor state shortly after quenching and favors a scenario in which the rapid shutdown of star formation is associated with depletion or removal of the molecular gas reservoir, rather than primarily with suppressed star formation efficiency while retaining a substantial molecular gas reservoir. Our results suggest that, if no substantial gas replenishment occurs in the future, dormant galaxies are more consistent with becoming "dead'' than with being temporarily "sleeping''.

papers.title: The Role of Environment in Shaping the Assembly Timelines of Massive Quiescent Galaxies at Cosmic Noon
papers.authors: Tianmu Gao, J. Trevor Mendel, Letizia Bugiani, Minjung Park, Sirio Belli, Joel Leja, Claudia del P. Lagos, Amir H. Khoram, Rebecca L. Davies, Razieh Emami, Gabriel Maheson, Anita Zanella, Benjamin P. Collins
papers.abstract: JWST observations of massive quiescent galaxies (MQGs) at $z\sim2$ have revealed diverse star formation histories (SFHs). In this letter, we investigate whether these variations are linked to the environment in which MQGs reside, as quantified by the host dark matter halo mass. We identify 12 MQGs from a representative sample of galaxies at $1.6<z<3.5$ obtained by the Blue Jay survey, a JWST Cycle 1 program, and infer their SFHs via modelling of the deep NIRSpec medium-resolution spectra along with multi-band photometry. By correlating the formation and quenching epochs of individual MQGs with their respective host halo masses from the 3D-HST survey, we find that after accounting for the redshift range of the sample ($1.8<z<2.5$), MQGs in more massive haloes formed at significantly earlier cosmic epochs. Meanwhile, although these galaxies also quenched earlier overall, the scatter in quenching epochs across similar halo masses indicates that the quenching process likely involves other contributing factors and is not solely determined by halo mass.

papers.title: The physical and chemical structure of TMC-1. The spatial distribution and excitation conditions of carbon, oxygen, and sulfur bearing species: Depletion of CO and CS
papers.authors: J. Cernicharo, B. Tercero, N. Marcelino, G. Esplugues, G. Molpeceres, M. Agúndez
papers.abstract: We present a detailed study of the physical and chemical structure of TMC-1 from the observed spatial distribution of HC3N, NNH+, CN, and their isotopologues, the O-bearing species C18O, C17O, CH3OH, CH3CHO, and H2CO, and the S-bearing species CS, HCS+, H2CS, and H2CCS. The well known filamentary structure of TMC-1 can be interpreted as a single cloud with a velocity gradient perpendicular to the filament, or less likely as due to the alignment of three independent clouds in the line sight with velocities of 5.3-5.7, 5.7-5.9, and 5.9-6.3 km/s. The main contribution to the emission of all studied C-bearing species is found at 5.83 kms/s. We conclude that the three velocity components are dynamically connected and that C-bearing molecules show a different behavior of their abundances compared to O-bearing species, which have emission peaks at 5.7 and 6.25 km/s, and appear at different spatial locations than cyanopolyynes and CnH and CnN radicals. The detection of 13C18O, with exactly the same line profile than that of C18O and C17O, excludes the possibility that the decrease of their emission at 5.83 km/s, could be due to self absorption or absorption by a foreground cloud component. Hence, as indicated by the spatial distribution of C18O and C17O, CO is significantly depleted at the velocities and positions where the emission of the carbon chains and radicals is found. This suggests that the emission of O-bearing species is coming from the external layers of the carbon-rich filaments. A comparison between S-bearing species and other molecules indicates that CS, CCS, HCS+, and H2CS are significantly depleted in the zone of CO depletion. A clear increase of the deuteration of several molecular species is found in the zones where CO and CS are depleted.

papers.title: Galactic Morpholography: Linking present-day galaxy compactness to assembly history and relic formation in the COLIBRE simulations
papers.authors: Maximilian Zemsch, Claudia D.P. Lagos, Chiara Spiniello, Michele Cappellari, Ángel Chandro-Gómez, Katy L. Proctor, Evgenii Chaikin, Johanna Hartke, Filip Huško, Sylvia Ploeckinger, Alexander J. Richings, Mahsa Sanati, Joop Schaye, James W. Trayford
papers.abstract: Compactness is widely used to identify candidate relic galaxies, the largely untouched survivors of the first compact massive galaxies. Yet relicness is an evolutionary rather than structural property. Using the COLIBRE cosmological hydrodynamical simulations, we test whether present-day structure traces galaxy formation and assembly histories. Six complementary tracers (stellar age, metallicity, [Mg/Fe], sSFR, velocity dispersion and ex-situ mass fraction) vary coherently across the stellar mass-size plane and independently identify a characteristic compactness scale of $\log_{10}(\Sigma_{1.5,\mathrm{crit}}/(\mathrm{M}_\odot\mathrm{kpc}^{-1.5}))=9.75\pm0.10$. We term this mapping between present-day structure and assembly history morpholography. Combining this threshold with the Degree of Relicness ($\mathrm{DoR}>0.6$), which quantifies early and rapid star formation, we distinguish compact from ancient galaxies and identify 267 relic candidates at their intersection. Ancient galaxies span nearly the full ex-situ-fraction range, from predominantly in-situ formation to substantial merger-driven growth. Relic candidates are concentrated at stellar masses of $\approx 10^{10}$-$10^{11}$ solar masses, host black holes that lie $\approx 0.25$-$2.5$ dex above the median black-hole-stellar-mass relation, and are predominantly satellites (76%), preferentially in cluster environments. Only $\approx 3$% show evidence of strong tidal stripping, suggesting that environment primarily preserves rather than creates relic-like systems. Approximately one third (87/267) are direct descendants of the $z=2$ massive quiescent galaxies identified in COLIBRE. Present-day structure thus retains a statistical fossil record of assembly history, supporting morpholography as a link between nearby galaxies and the early Universe.

papers.title: Uncovering the origin of complex velocity distributions in edge-on disc galaxies
papers.authors: Sophie Townson, Marie Martig, Robert J. J. Grand, Prashin Jethwa, Jesús Falcón-Barroso, Timothy A. Davis
papers.abstract: Stellar line-of-sight velocity distributions are a powerful tool for studying galaxy kinematics and formation history, with multiple-peaked LOSVDs often indicating the presence of complex kinematic components. We extract stellar LOSVDs across the disc of a simulated spiral galaxy viewed edge-on, and study how often and why we see multiple-peaked LOSVDs. We find that the multiple-peaked LOSVDs are mainly found close to the midplane because they result from the presence of spiral arms. This is not because the spiral arms have significantly different kinematics to the disc, but because they correspond to over-densities. Variations in the number of arms present along a line-of-sight create variations in the number of peaks in LOSVDs. This can be used to quantify the strength of the spiral arms above the midplane, and how the thickness of spiral arms vary across the disc. We find that the commonly used fourth order Gauss-Hermite moment, $h_4$, is negative in the regions where there are multiple-peaked LOSVDs, and hence traces spiral arms. Finally, we discuss the observability of the multiple-peaked regions and their associated $h_4$ measurements with current integral field spectrographs. We find that the spectral resolution of MUSE might not be high enough to uncover multiple peaks in LOSVDs when they result from spiral arms, but should allow for identification of the regions of negative $h_4$. On the other hand, higher resolution spectrographs like KOALA and WEAVE may be able to recover multiple peaks in LOSVDs, representing a promising avenue for characterising spiral arms in edge-on disc galaxies.

papers.title: Constrain the Size of Broad Line Region in NGC 1068 Using Sub-millimeter Excess
papers.authors: Qi Guo, Junzhi Wang, Lingrui Lin, Yuqiang Li, Zhi-yu Zhang, Fengyao Zhu
papers.abstract: Constraining the size of broad-line region (BLR) close to the accretion disk in active galactic nuclei (AGNs) is key to understand the central engine and evolution of AGN. We propose a new method to constrain the BLR size, based on millimeter to sub-millimeter spectral energy distribution (SED), from which a sub-millimeter excess may be found. Such excess can be used to determine the solid angle of the free-free emission region from BLR, as a region with high electron density and optically thick at sub-millimeter wavelength for free-free continuum. Millimeter to sub-millimeter SED analysis toward the central source S1 in a nearby type II AGN NGC 1068 was done, which gave an upper limit on the solid angle of BLR region as(4.94 +/- 0.61) *10^-6 arcsec^2, corresponding to a radius no more than 0.085 pc. Such a constraint on the BLR size is important for estimating the masses of central supermassive black holes in AGNs.

papers.title: The ringing Large Magellanic Cloud: evidence for a recent dwarf-dwarf collision
papers.authors: Slater J. Oden, Bethany Garver, Joshua Povick, David L. Nidever, Victor P. Debattista
papers.abstract: Galaxy interactions are ubiquitous in the Universe and represent a primary pathway for galaxy growth. Close passages of dwarf galaxies can induce large-scale vertical oscillations in stellar disks, a phenomenon first identified in the Milky Way within the past decade. Here, we use recent red clump distance maps of the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) to show that its stellar periphery is vertically offset from the central disk plane by $\sim$1.2 kpc at radii of $\sim$8.5 kpc and exhibits an S-shaped warp reaching $\sim$3.6 kpc at $\sim$11.5 kpc. We compare these observations to an $N$-body simulation of the LMC-Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) system, in which a direct collision between the Clouds excites vertical oscillations in the outer LMC disk with amplitudes of $\sim$1~kpc and a period of $\sim$600~Myr. The simulated disk best matches the observed vertical structure $\sim$260~Myr after the collision, although this timing depends on the adopted LMC model. At that time, the simulation reproduces the sign and radial onset of the observed offset and the orientation of the warp, but underpredicts the amplitude of the warp by a factor of $\sim$4-5. These results support a collision-driven origin for the large-scale vertical structure of the LMC disk and demonstrate that dwarf--dwarf interactions can reshape stellar disks on galactic scales.

papers.title: IRAC-Excess Galaxies in the NIRSpec Wide Survey: physical properties of bright EELGs at $z\sim7$ and implications for Reionization
papers.authors: Katherine Ormerod, Renske Smit, Joris Witstok, Anna de Graaff, Michael V. Maseda, Andrew J. Bunker, Chris Willott
papers.abstract: We present an analysis of 23 Spitzer/IRAC excess galaxies at $5.66 < z < 7.64$, observed as part of the NIRSpec Wide GTO survey. With NIRSpec PRISM spectroscopy, we measure a median rest-frame [OIII]$+\rm{H}\beta$ EW $=1583$~Å, consistent with predictions from the pre-JWST selection and we identify $17/23$ $(\sim74\%)$ of our sample as extreme emission line galaxies (EELGs), based on a selection of [OIII]$+\rm{H}\beta$ EW $\geq1000$~Å. The typical EELG is powered by star-formation rather than active galactic nuclei (AGN) based on their line widths, line ratios and absence of high-ionization lines, though we cannot exclude an AGN contribution in a few individual sources. We find that our luminous ($\langle M_\mathrm{UV}\rangle=-20.7$) EELG sample is characterised by sub-solar metallicities $(7.38 < \rm 12 + \log(O/H) < 8.12)$, young stellar populations ($t_\star \sim 20$ Myr), and enhanced ionizing photon production efficiencies, with median $\log_{10}(\xi_\mathrm{ion}/\mathrm{erg}^{-1}~\mathrm{Hz}) = 25.62$. We find that more UV luminous ($\sim L_\mathrm{UV, z=7}^\ast$) EELGs exhibit systematically lower O32 ratios than fainter ($\sim 0.1\times L_\mathrm{UV}^\ast$) EELGs at fixed [OIII]$+\rm{H}\beta$ EW, indicating less extreme radiation fields and/or lower gas densities than their fainter counterparts. Furthermore, bright EELGs exhibit low neutral hydrogen column densities, consistent with a scenario in which they have largely ionized their circumgalactic medium (CGM). Despite this, we find very low Lyman-$\alpha$ escape fractions ($<2$\%), suggesting these systems reside in relatively small ($\lesssim 0.25$~pMpc) ionized regions of the intergalactic medium (IGM), possibly suggesting that bright galaxies have a minor contribution to reionization.

papers.title: The contact frontier in Galactic civilization networks: radial structure and the Galactic habitable zone
papers.authors: Kohji Tsumura
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; Earth and Planetary Astrophysics (astro-ph.EP); Instrumentation and Methods for Astrophysics (astro-ph.IM)
papers.abstract: The probability of interstellar contact depends not only on the abundance of technological civilizations but also on their spatial connectivity. Treating civilizations as nodes linked whenever their separation is smaller than the distance a signal travels within a communicative lifetime, we determine the radial structure of Galactic civilization networks. An exponential stellar disc replaces the uniform disc of earlier work, and the fraction of stars hosting civilizations may vary with radius as a Galactic Habitable Zone (GHZ). The isolation, contact and network transitions are frontiers several kiloparsecs wide, not boundaries: the contact frontier is set entirely by the disc scale length, and the network frontier, broadened by gradient percolation, stays near 1.5 scale lengths. The two frontiers overlap over a band containing the Sun, where both transitions proceed at once. Within this factorized GHZ model, the radius of peak civilization density depends only logarithmically on the strength of supernova sterilization, and the wide range of published peak radii, from the Galactic centre to 12 kpc, is reproduced primarily by varying that one parameter. Under the present normalization, the location of the zone has only a modest effect on the local contact probability, whereas the modelled Galactic connectivity is minimized when the civilization-density peak lies near the solar Galactocentric radius, where current determinations place the peak.

papers.title: A Step-Like Transition Underlying the Life and Death of Galaxies
papers.authors: Zhicheng He, Enci Wang, Luis C. Ho, Yingjie Peng, Huiyuan Wang, Yong Shi, Tao Wang, Yongquan Xue, Tinggui Wang
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; Cosmology and Nongalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)
papers.abstract: How galaxies stop forming stars is a complex and central problem in astrophysics. Numerous physical mechanisms have been proposed, yet a simple, unified framework connecting these mechanisms remains lacking. Here, we derive a step-function quenching response from the fundamental principle of gas mass conservation, governed by the competition between gas-supply and gas-depletion timescales. This response also enables the gas-supply timescale to be inferred from the observed quenched fraction. Applying this method to approximately 350,000 galaxies, we find a characteristic gas-supply timescale of ~1 Gyr, reveal distinct inside-out and outside-in quenching signatures associated with supermassive black holes and dark matter halos, respectively, and identify galaxies with intermediate stellar surface mass densities as occupying a critical state for quenching and rejuvenation. Our work establishes a unified physical framework in which a simple step-function response captures how diverse physical processes regulate galaxy quenching and the resumption of star formation through their effects on the competition between gas-supply and gas-depletion timescales.

papers.title: Binary-lens amplification of starlight: from magnification flares to quasi-periodic tracking of orbital evolution
papers.authors: Hanxi Wang, Bence Kocsis, Miguel Zumalacárregui
papers.subjects: Astrophysics of Galaxies (astro-ph.GA) ; Cosmology and Nongalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO); General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology (gr-qc)
papers.abstract: Supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHB) are expected at the center of galaxies as a result of galaxy mergers. The dynamics and evolution of SMBHBs shed light on the evolution and formation of galaxies, the gravitational wave background and the nature of gravity. Many methods have been proposed to identify sub-parsec SMBHBs via the detection of gravitational waves or the modulation of the emission from the surrounding gaseous environment. In a previous study, we proposed a new method of identifying SMBHBs in non-active galactic nuclei via gravitational lensing. The caustics, i.e. the source positions with a divergent magnification, exhibit a complex extended geometry which rotates with the binary period. Each caustic-crossing produces an extreme magnification by up to a factor of $10^{6}$. In this work, we generalize the previous study and describe the rich phenomenology of binary-lens amplification of starlight (BLAST). We explore the electromagnetic transients produced when accounting for the relative proper motion of the source, either a single or a binary star, the eccentricity and precession of the SMBHB, and the relative inclination. Systems where a star rapidly drifts across the caustic produce a single- or double-peaked flare. In the opposite limit, a star with no relative proper motion produces quasi-periodic lensed starlight (QPLS), i.e., repeated peaks that track the system's orbital evolution. We determine the expected magnification and peak duration in different circumstances, and calculate the magnification curves and their Fourier transforms. This study may help construct search pipelines to identify SMBHBs in electromagnetic time-domain surveys.
